exposure: Biochemical and hematological parameters (CRP, band cell count)
outcome: Diagnosis of early-onset severe neonatal infections (sepsis, congenital pneumonia, severe urinary tract infection)
cohort: The study included 129 neonates, comprising 89 with early-onset severe infections (52 preterm, 37 full-term) and 40 healthy neonates (25 full-term, 15 preterm) as a control group.
finding: Serum RANTES concentration (sRC) was significantly higher in infected neonates (both full-term and preterm) compared to healthy controls, and sRC positively correlated with CRP value and band cell count.
cross-section timing: Early-onset period in neonates for diagnosis of infections
gest_age: Preterm and full-term neonates were included and analyzed separately.
